title: Integral functor and Roos-value comparisons for arbitrary proper compactifications
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D with geometric field k [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime l different from D.p, a proper k-scheme Y [def-weil-proper-morphism], a compactification c of its structure map a:Y→Spec k, and a finite extension E of Q_l [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let F_c be the recorded integral compact-support functor [def-weil-compact-support-finite-action] and let C_c(K), I(K) be the recorded compact and ordinary integral image values [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. Then F_c followed by the full-subcategory inclusion is naturally isomorphic to the inclusion followed by completed ordinary derived direct image [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. For every integral constructible K, C_c(K) is isomorphic to I(K) in the integral constructible category. The coefficient sheaves, quotient transitions and chosen Roos values are exactly those of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support].

source.place: first paragraph: identity compactification and passage through coefficients

proof.text: Compare c with the identity compactification on the coherent quotient system using the normalized proper finite comparisons. Their quotient restriction square identifies all adjacent transitions, so this is an isomorphism of systems, rather than an inference from unrelated level isomorphisms.

At the identity compactification the identity-open extension cancels on the entire system. The integral tower comparison applies the same total-derived-limit functor and preserves its actual projections. Transport through the recorded compact-support realization. Ordinary direct image of a complete input commutes with that limit by its right adjunction, giving the displayed natural comparison with completed ordinary derived direct image.

For each K, the recorded compact and ordinary objects are vertices of Roos triangles for the two compared towers. The compatible term isomorphism identifies the products and their one-minus-shift maps. Rotate the two triangles, extend the product arrow isomorphism to a triangle isomorphism and unshift its third component. This identifies their vertices. Lift the isomorphism to the full constructible subcategory. Zero and empty cases are the zero towers; every positive exponent, including one, occurs.

proof_origin.place: expanded coefficient passage and recorded-value identifications

theorem properCompactIntegralComparisons
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (Y : Scheme.{u})
    [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k))]
    [IsProper (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k))]
    (c : Compactification (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k)))
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] :
    letI : (Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k)).Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k)) := ⟨𝟙 _⟩
    Nonempty (sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor l D.k (finiteFieldDatumPrimeUnit D l hl)
        c E ⋙ (sfIntegralConstructible l E (Spec (.of D.k))).ι ≅
      (sfIntegralConstructible l E Y).ι ⋙
        sfCompletedDerivedDirectImage l E (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))) ∧
    ∀ K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E Y,
      Nonempty (sfIntegralCompactSupportValue l E D.k (finiteFieldDatumPrimeUnit D l hl)
        c K ≅ integralImage D l hl E Y K)
